page: Amazon Web Services c6g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton processors based on the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a 1:1 vCPU-to-physical-core mapping without simultaneous multithreading. Hardware cache allocation includes 64 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, alongside 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

Benchmark evaluations show stable multi-threaded execution across common server tasks. The platform achieves a stress-ng multi-core score of 24286.42 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 8581.0, alongside steady performance in clang software compilation (15859.0) and ray tracing (13820.0). Static web serving throughput reaches 18.73 GB/sec, while in-memory operations register 19.74 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded metrics remain modest, with a Geekbench single-core score of 969.0, limited gzip compression throughput, and subpar scores in PassMark CPU encryption tests.

The hardware configuration omits local disk storage, requiring network-attached Amazon EBS volumes for persistent filesystems. Network performance provides a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. No dedicated GPU accelerators are present, which restricts performance for machine learning inference; testing indicates weak to poor token processing across small and medium language models.

The Graviton-based architecture offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for scaled multi-threaded workloads, exchanging peak single-core performance for lower power consumption and higher core density. The instance is suited for multi-threaded batch processing, microservices, containerized applications, software compilation, static web serving, and distributed caching layers.
description: Amazon Web Services c6g.4xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated physical cores of AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 silicon clocked at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a 5 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, utilizing the Nitro hypervisor and network-attached block storage instead. Benchmarks indicate balanced multi-threaded compute, showing 24286.42 in stress-ng multi-core and 19.74 million Redis SET operations per second, contrasted by modest single-threaded throughput and reduced cryptographic benchmark results. It provides a cost-efficient resource density profile well-aligned with distributed services, software compilation, static web serving, and containerized backend fleets.
